I've confirmed the file layout; let me write the answer from the actual SE-2 transport code and Next.js build semantics."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":875,"cache_read_input_tokens":21300,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":875},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"534e58cf-6e72-4072-8bb1-49eed4e3557d","uuid":"c2381b5d-ade4-424c-a147-626d7c2c75c6","timestamp":"2026-07-24T15:14:46.364Z","request_id":"req_011CdM6kkWvaGC697F3iU3gN"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdM6kmD6Z2FU32gjnANVp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01L5GyJHbbNzjwMdoWtvCNZ1","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/qa-quiz-005/2026-07-24T151334Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why production requests land on `mainnet.base.org`\n\n## TL;DR\n\n`NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` is **inlined at build time**, not read at runtime. The\nproduction static bundle was built in an environment where that variable was\n**not set**, so `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` was frozen into the client JS\nas `undefined`. With the override missing, SE-2's transport falls back to a bare\n`http()`, and viem's bare `http()` resolves to the chain's **default public RPC**\n— for Base that is `https://mainnet.base.org`. Hence the 429s. Dev machines have\nthe variable in `.env.local`, so their build inlines the paid URL and never\ntouches the public endpoint.\n\n---\n\n## The exact chain\n\n### 1. `scaffold.config.ts` reads the env var\n```ts\nrpcOverrides: {\n  [chains.base.id]: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL,\n},\n```\nThis is not \"read the RPC URL.\" It's \"read the value of `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL`\n**at the moment the code is compiled**.\"\n\n### 2. Next.js inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` at build time\nAny identifier `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FOO` in code that ends up in the browser\nbundle is **textually substituted** by Next.js's webpack `DefinePlugin` during\n`next build`. It is not a runtime lookup. Two consequences:\n\n- Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_`-prefixed vars are exposed to the browser at all.\n- The value is **whatever was in the shell/`.env` when `next build` ran**, baked\n  in as a string literal. If the var is absent at build time, the substitution\n  is literally `undefined`.\n\nSo after build, `rpcOverrides[base.id]` is a **constant** in the shipped JS —\neither `\"https://paid-rpc...\"` or `undefined`. Nothing on the server can change\nit later.\n\n### 3. Dev vs. production diverge here\n- **Dev machines**: `.env.local` (or `.env`) contains `NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL=<paid>`.\n  `next dev`/`next build` inlines the paid URL → override present → paid RPC. No 429s.\n- **Production static build**: the deploy is a **static Next.js build on generic\n  hosting**. The var was almost certainly **not present in the build/CI\n  environment** (or was set only in the hosting platform's *runtime* env, which a\n  static build never reads). It inlines as `undefined`. Setting the variable in\n  the host's runtime dashboard does nothing — there is no server process\n  re-reading env for `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`; the value is already frozen in the static\n  chunks.\n\n### 4. `wagmiConfig.tsx` transport with the override missing\n```ts\nclient({ chain }) {\n  let rpcFallbacks = [http()];                                   // <-- default\n\n  const rpcOverrideUrl = scaffoldConfig.rpcOverrides?.[chain.id];\n  if (rpcOverrideUrl) {\n    rpcFallbacks = [http(rpcOverrideUrl), http()];\n  } else {\n    // alchemy default-key branch, still ends with a bare http()\n  }\n\n  return createClient({ chain, transport: fallback(rpcFallbacks, { rank: false }), ... });\n}\n```\nWith `rpcOverrideUrl === undefined`, the `if` is skipped and the base client\nkeeps `rpcFallbacks = [http()]`.\n\n### 5. What a bare `http()` does\n`http(url?)` with **no URL** does not throw and does not disable the chain. viem\nfalls back to `chain.rpcUrls.default.http[0]`. For viem's `base` chain that is\n**`https://mainnet.base.org`** — the public endpoint. Under production traffic\nthat endpoint rate-limits → **429**.\n\nThat is the whole loop: missing build-time var → `undefined` override →\n`http()` with no arg → viem's Base default public RPC → 429.\n\n---\n\n## The one operational check that settles whether the fix is real\n\n**Inspect the actual RPC host in the shipped artifact, not the config or the\nhosting dashboard.** Concretely, either:\n\n- Open the production site, DevTools → **Network**, and confirm the JSON-RPC\n  POSTs go to the **paid host**, not `mainnet.base.org`; or equivalently\n- `grep -r \"mainnet.base.org\\|<paid-rpc-host>\" .next/static` (or the deployed\n  `_next/static` chunks) and confirm the **paid URL is baked in** and the public\n  one is not the one being called.\n\nWhy this and nothing else: because the value is inlined at build time, the only\nproof that the fix works is that the **paid URL is present in the deployed client\nbundle / actual live requests**. Changing `.env`, setting the var in the host\ndashboard, or \"it's set in CI now\" prove nothing until you **rebuild and\nredeploy** and see the paid host in the bundle/Network tab. The fix is real iff\nthe shipped JS calls the paid RPC.\n\n---\n\n## The second, transport-level trap (persists even after the env var is fixed)\n\nLook at the override branch itself:\n```ts\nrpcFallbacks = [http(rpcOverrideUrl), http()];\n//                                    ^^^^^^  bare http() = public RPC\n```\nEven once the paid URL is correctly inlined, the transport is a viem\n`fallback([ paid, public ])`. The **second entry is a bare `http()`**, i.e. the\nsame public `mainnet.base.org`. viem's `fallback` transport routes to the next\ntransport whenever the current one **errors** — including on timeouts, 5xx, and\ncrucially **429 rate-limit responses**. So under load, or any hiccup on the paid\nendpoint, a share of requests **still spill onto the public RPC**, which can then\n429 in turn. The public endpoint is never removed from the routing set; it's\ndemoted to failover, not eliminated.\n\n(Related, same root cause: SE-2 always appends `mainnet` to `enabledChains` for\nENS/price lookups, and `rpcOverrides` only covers `base.id`. The mainnet client\nhas no override, so its `rpcFallbacks` also ends in a bare `http()` → public\nmainnet RPC. Different host, same \"bare `http()` = public\" trap.)\n\n**To actually stop public-RPC traffic**, drop the trailing bare `http()` from the\nfallback array (or replace it with a second *paid/keyed* endpoint), and provide\nan override for every enabled chain — including the implicitly-added mainnet —\nrather than leaving a public endpoint in the transport at all.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":875,"cache_read_input_tokens":21300,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":875},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"534e58cf-6e72-4072-8bb1-49eed4e3557d","uuid":"cd49deab-7cd4-44f2-812e-acf1c000273f","timestamp":"2026-07-24T15:15:18.613Z","request_id":"req_011CdM6kkWvaGC697F3iU3gN"}
